title: I Come from a Misty Far Country
text:
I come from a misty far country,

ruled by an old sad monarch...

My muse seeks only what is arcane,

my muse adores only what does not exist.


You weep for a dream that is far away,

you await an affection that no longer exists,

your pupils lose themselves in the arcane

like two black wings, and you are very sad.


You are mine: we were born of the same arcane

and we go, disdainful of all that exists,

in pursuit of that misty far country,

ruled by an old sad monarch...
editorial_note: The translation keeps the refrain-like arcane country and its melancholy kinship.

title: Autobiography
text:
Autobiographical verses? There are my songs,

there are my poems: I, like fortunate

nations, and following the example of the honorable woman,

have no history: nothing has ever happened to me,

oh noble unknown friend, that I could tell you.


Back in my young years I divined in Art

the harmony and rhythm, dear to the Muse-leader,

and, able to be rich, I preferred to be a poet.


—And afterward?


—I suffered, like everyone, and loved.


Much?


—Enough to be forgiven...
editorial_note: The translation keeps the witty autobiography built from art, suffering, love, and pardon.

title: Cowardice
text:
She passed with her mother. What rare beauty!

What blond hair of bluish wheat!

What rhythm in her step! What innate royalty

of bearing! What forms beneath the fine tulle...!


She passed with her mother. She turned her head:

her blue gaze pierced me very deep!


I remained as in ecstasy...

With feverish haste,

"Follow her!" body and soul cried together.


...But I was afraid to love madly,

to open my wounds, which often bleed,

and despite all my thirst for tenderness,

closing my eyes, I let her pass!
editorial_note: The translation keeps the moment of erotic recognition undone by fear.

title: To Nemesis
text:
Your arm hurls me into sorrow,

you steal all that recreates my soul,

and I have almost nothing: flower that your simoom

breath airs, withers for me.


But my faith grows beside my grief,

and I say like the Just Man of Idumea:

God wills it so, blessed be He!

The Lord gives it to me, He takes it from me.


Let your fury prosper, nothing matters to me:

I can do all things in THAT ONE who comforts me,

and I resign myself to the mourning that kills me;


because, red vision in dark night,

Christ goes along my way of bitterness

shaking his scarlet tunic.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the Job-like resignation and the capitalized source of strength.

title: Your Arm Hurls Me into Sorrow...
text:
Your arm hurls me into sorrow,

you steal all that recreates my soul,

and I have almost nothing: flower that your simoom

breath airs, withers for me.


But my faith grows beside my grief,

and I say like the Just Man of Idumea:

God wills it so, blessed be He!

The Lord gives it to me, He takes it from me.


Let your fury prosper, nothing matters to me:

I can do all things in THAT ONE who comforts me,

and I resign myself to the mourning that kills me;


because, red vision in dark night,

Christ goes along my way of bitterness

shaking his scarlet tunic.
editorial_note: This first-line version keeps the same prayerful endurance under Nemesis.

title: If You Say to Me: "Come!", I Leave Everything
text:
If you say to me: "Come!", I leave everything...

I will not even turn my gaze back

to look at the beloved woman...

But say it to me strongly, in such a way


that your voice, like a call to assembly,

vibrates even in the most intimate recess

of being, lifts the soul from its mire

and wounds the heart like a sword.


If you say to me: "Come!", I leave everything.

I will arrive at your sanctuary almost old,

and in the gleam of twilight light;


but I must compensate you for my delay,

by diffusing myself, oh Christ!, like a tuberose

of subtle perfume, before your altar.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the call to Christ as both martial summons and fragrant surrender.

title: So Blond Is the Girl That
text:
So blond is the girl

that when there is sun, she cannot be seen.


It seems she diffuses herself

in the morning ray,

that with the light is confused

her crystal silhouette,

tinted in roses, and it seems

that in the clarity of day

she fades away,

my girl.


If my Damiana leans out

at the window, and dawn colors

her fresh complexion

of apricot and velvet,

one does not know if dawn

has come out to the window

before coming out to the sky.


Damiana in the blush

of the little morning

dissolves and, if the sun rises,

because she is blond... she cannot be seen.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the girl's blondness merging with dawn and sunlight.

title: To Philip II
text:
I do not know what current of asceticism,

what relation, what impure affinity

linked your sadness and my sadness

and joined your idealism and my idealism.


But I know by intuition that one same star

has presided over our dark night,

and that in me as in you the height wages

a fatal combat with the abyss.


Oh king; you are my king! Sullen and fierce

I too am; in a sea of arcane mourning

my luminous spirit loses itself,


and I hide like you, proud and mute,

beneath the black velvet doublet,

the implacable cancer that bites me.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the severe kinship between the speaker and Philip II.

title: The Cloudglow
text:
Where did you go, Love, where did you go?

The gentle fire went out in the west,

and you, who told me: "until later,

I will return by night"... did not return!


In what brambles did you wound your divine foot?

What cruel wall deafened you to my plea?

What snow knew how to freeze your attachment

and steal from your memory my sad image?


...Love, you will not come now! In vain, anxious,

from my balcony I live watching

the green field and the misty boundary;


and a fugitive cloudglow feigns for me

a ship of light in which, toward final rest,

your sweet thoughtful phantom goes.
editorial_note: The translation uses cloudglow for celaje to keep the luminous sunset apparition.

title: You Pass through the Abyss of My Sorrows
text:
You pass through the abyss of my sorrows

like a moonbeam over the seas,

anointing the infinity of my griefs

with the tuberose and myrrh of your tendernesses.


My life is already setting, yours begins;

but, leaping over the barriers of time,

like a moonbeam over the seas,

you pass through the abyss of my sorrows.


No more on the smoothness of my songs

will disenchantment leave its roughnesses;

for God, who gave the heavens their luminaries,

wanted you to cross through my sorrows

like a moonbeam over the seas.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the refrain of the beloved as moonbeam crossing sorrow.
